questions: Does max_error move below 0.06 m with the row at y = 0.02 m, or does it stay near 0.061 to 0.064 m?
Does oval steering_oscillation stay at or below about 0.2 from 0.181, or does the closer reaction point raise it?
Does oval progress stay near 0.34, or rise? If it stays below 0.35, is speed the limit so that wheel_radius 0.035 m is the next lever?
Does the closer row lose the line on the slalom or s-bend, given line_loss_events was 0.25 on the slalom at y = 0.03 m?

intent: Test the reaction point in isolation. Move the seven-sensor row from y = 0.03 m to y = 0.02 m, keeping the 0.10 m track, 0.8 kg mass, 0.16 m body and 0.03 m wheels from iteration 4. Expected: max_error falls below about 0.06 m, oval steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.2, and line_loss_events stays near 0. If progress stays below 0.35, the next test is wheel_radius 0.035 m.
learning: Iteration 4 showed that restoring mass and body length (inertia about 0.0027) brought oval oscillation down to 0.181 while keeping the 0.10 m track. Track width did not drive oscillation, and inertia did. max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.064 m through every change so far. This race tests whether the reaction point moves that floor. If it does not, geometry has little left to fix max_error, and the controller needs the next move.
rationale: Iteration 4 (0.8 kg, 0.16 m body, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 16 mm sensors at y = 0.03 m) is the first race that meets the Integrator's conditions for a reaction-point test. Oval steering_oscillation fell to 0.181, below the 0.2 threshold, so restoring inertia cured the jitter that the light robot had. Line loss is 0 on the oval and s-bend, and only 0.25 events per run on the slalom. Max_error stayed at 0.0614 m, so every run still leaves the 0.06 m floor. Body width cannot raise that floor, because the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) and this stays at 0.06 for all allowed widths. Tracking therefore has to improve, and the reaction point is the remaining untested geometry lever. Across iterations 0 to 4, max_error has sat at 0.062 to 0.064 m whatever the track, mass or sensor footprint, so the reaction point is the variable I have not yet moved in isolation. Progress on the oval is 0.34, below the Integrator's 0.35 threshold for a speed test. I will not test wheel radius in this same race, because it would confound the reaction-point result, and wheel radius is the next lever if progress stays low. This iteration changes only the sensor row, from y = 0.03 m to y = 0.02 m, which brings the row closer to the axle and so reduces the lead the controller has on the line. Everything else is held at the iteration 4 values. Expected result: max_error falls below about 0.06 m, or at least moves materially, while oval oscillation stays near or below 0.2 and line_loss_events stays near 0. If max_error does not move, the controller gain is the limit, not geometry.
